tool.name: Salmon quantmerge
tool.description: Merge multiple quantification results into a single file
tool.command:
#import re
#for $counter, $input_data in enumerate($quants): mkdir ${counter}.quantmerge && ln -s '${input_data}' ${counter}.quantmerge/quant.sf && #end for salmon --no-version-check quantmerge --quants #for $counter, $input_data in enumerate($quants): ${counter}.quantmerge #end for --names #for $input_data in $quants: #set $identifier = re.sub('[^\w\-]', '_', str($input_data.element_identifier)) '${identifier}' #end for --column '${column}' ${genes} #if str($missing) != "None": --missing '${missing}' #end if -o qmergeout.tab

param.label: Salmon quant tabular output files
param.help: Select multiple quant.sf files (e.g. the outputs of Salmon quant); the column names of the merged matrix are derived from the dataset identifiers

param.label: Columns
param.help: Name of columns that will be merged in the output file

param.label: Genes
param.help: Use gene quantifications instead of transcript

tool.help:
@salmonhelp@
-----
**Input datasets**
Multiple `quant.sf` files may be selected at once; a list collection of `quant.sf` files (for example the output of a Salmon quant step run on a collection of samples) can be handed to the input as well, in which case a single merged TPM, NumReads or length matrix is produced.
The column headers of the merged matrix are derived from the dataset identifiers; every character that is not a letter, a digit, an underscore or a hyphen is replaced by `_`.
